content.text:
## What works

- `ui/audio-stream.js:40` preserves resampling phase: `this.phase-=consumed`. The renderer keeps continuity across transport blocks; the retained browser report records `worstResidual: 0.00003605582369417201` (`artifacts/audio/browser-8209c64b13644d59896f8070c3a4db36/report.json:40`). This is inspected evidence, not a test rerun.
- `scripts/crow_native_patch.py:15` copies received bytes into each event: `memcpy(ev->crow_event.line, ...)`. This fixes the shared-buffer ownership problem without replacing native Crow transport.
- `src/runtime/audio_capture.py:51` rejects nonzero `xruns`, `nonfinite` and `server_dead` metrics before declaring completion. Capturing a WAV alone cannot produce a successful result.

## What doesn't work

- **[MAJOR] Enabling ii turns harmless CV diagnostics into fatal errors.** `src/devices/crow_ii_host/main.c:18` unconditionally sets `failed=1` for wrapped `printf`; line 20 does the same for `puts`. These wrappers apply to the entire combined host (`scripts/build_crow_host.py:33`), including official CASL’s ordinary `printf("do nothing\n")` (`.runtime/crow-feasibility/crow/lib/casl.c:356`). Configure `output[1].action=adsr()`, trigger it, then release twice: the redundant release terminates the ii-enabled backend instead of preserving upstream behavior. Restrict fatal handling to actual error paths, retaining the queue-overflow negative test.

- **[MAJOR] Instant ASL completion callbacks are silently lost.** `src/devices/crow_host/main.c:60` takes `counts[c]=done[c]` immediately before stepping, and line 63 dispatches only subsequent increments. Official CASL completes zero-duration actions synchronously through `L_queue_asl_done(index)` (`.runtime/crow-feasibility/crow/lib/casl.c:399`), so `output[1].action=to(5,0); output[1]()` increments the counter during the serial command, before the next snapshot. Voltage changes, but its registered `.done` callback never arrives. Retain pending completions across loop iterations and drain them with bounded dispatch; test an instant action through native Crow callbacks.

- **[MAJOR] Asynchronous Crow callbacks do not drain ii commands.** During normal operation, `flush(L)` runs only after a received serial newline (`src/devices/crow_host/main.c:75–79`); input and output callbacks execute separately at lines 59–64. A Crow-side change callback calling `ii.jf.play_note(0,5)` therefore leaves its packet queued until another serial command arrives; repeated stream callbacks eventually overflow the queue. Official firmware calls `ii_leader_process()` every event-loop iteration (`.runtime/crow-feasibility/crow/main.c:86`). Service the queue independently of serial reception and test callback-generated packets without sending a follow-up command. Existing key-driven ii tests do not exercise this path.

- **[MAJOR] Candidate composition can bless changed Crow Lua as pinned official source.** `scripts/build_audio_candidate.py:73` creates `lua_files` by hashing whatever currently occupies `crow_source/'lua'`, while line 30 verifies only the previously built executable. Editing `lua/output.lua` after building Crow but before building the audio candidate produces a manifest that retains the official pin and accepts the edited Lua at launch. This contradicts the claimed “canonical identified experimental build”; `scripts/prepare_crow_runtime.py:20` has the same re-baselining behavior. Record Lua identities when validating/building Crow, then verify and carry those identities through composition instead of generating new expectations.

## Risks

Nothing notable.

## Gaps

Nothing notable.

## Improvements

Nothing notable.
